physics.note: No physics option differs from bodies/horse.xml's own <option timestep="0.002" integrator="implicitfast"/> -- our Sim config only sets simulation_timestep, to the same 0.002 already in the XML (a no-op match, not an override); nothing else (integrator, solver, iterations, gravity, ...) is touched, so whatever horse.xml specifies (or MuJoCo's own compiled defaults, for anything horse.xml doesn't set) applies as-is. control_timestep=0.02 is not a MuJoCo physics option -- it's 10 physics substeps (at 0.002 each) per action/control step; actions are held constant (the position actuator's ctrl target) across those 10 substeps.
physics.engine_caveat: Training ran on mujoco_warp (GPU). If the browser's MuJoCo WASM build is the canonical CPU solver rather than warp, both implement the same model/options but we have not verified they are bit-exact with each other -- treat small numerical drift between engines as expected, not a bug, and the policy_reference samples below as the ground truth to diff against.

free_joint.name: root
free_joint.qpos_layout: [x, y, z, qw, qx, qy, qz] -- MuJoCo's native quaternion order (w first), world frame position.
free_joint.qvel_layout: [vx, vy, vz, wx, wy, wz] -- linear part (0:3) is WORLD frame; angular part (3:6) is BODY (torso-local) frame. This is MuJoCo's standard free-joint qvel convention, not something we changed.

initial_pose_by_start_type.drop: position (0, 0, z), z ~ Uniform(0.4, 0.8); orientation fully uniform-random over SO(3) (Shoemake's method -- no bias toward any landing side); qvel zero.
initial_pose_by_start_type.chest (sternal): position (0, 0, z), z ~ Uniform(0.35, 0.45); orientation = identity (torso's local up aligned with world up) rotated by a small random tilt (random unit axis, angle ~ Uniform(-0.26, 0.26) rad, ~+/-15 deg); qvel zero.
initial_pose_by_start_type.standing: position (0, 0, z), z ~ Uniform(0.75, 0.95); orientation = identity rotated by a smaller random tilt (angle ~ Uniform(-0.15, 0.15) rad, ~+/-8.6 deg); qvel zero.

qpos_qvel_joint_order: qpos[0:7] / qvel[0:6] are the free joint (see above). qpos[7:25] and qvel[6:24] are the 18 hinge joints, one qpos/qvel each, in exactly JOINT_NAMES order (confirmed against the compiled model's own qposadr/dofadr -- not assumed): ['neck-bend', 'neck-pitch', 'head-pitch', 'head-roll', 'fl-splay', 'fl-swing', 'fl-lower', 'fr-splay', 'fr-swing', 'fr-lower', 'spine-bend', 'spine-twist', 'hl-splay', 'hl-swing', 'hl-lower', 'hr-splay', 'hr-swing', 'hr-lower']
observation_layout: 60-vector = joint_pos(18) + joint_vel(18) + gravity_b(3) + ang_vel(3) + last_action(18), in that order, each block in JOINT_NAMES order where applicable. gravity_b is the world -z direction rotated into the torso body frame; ang_vel is torso angular velocity in the torso body frame; last_action is the previous step's raw policy output (pre scale/offset/clip). See policy.json for the full action -> ctrl scale/offset/clip.
action_to_ctrl: ctrl = clip(action * scale + offset, ctrlrange_lo, ctrlrange_hi), per joint -- see policy.json for the arrays.
action_magnitude_note: Checkpoint 9499's raw onnx_action values are large (seen up to roughly +/-47 across these samples, vs. roughly +/-1-3 in runs 1-2) -- v3 removed the energy/joint_speed penalties that used to keep actions small, and action_rate alone doesn't bound raw magnitude, just consecutive differences. In practice this means ctrl is usually fully saturated at one joint-range bound or the other (clip() does the real work), not a smooth mid-range target. Checked against the torch policy directly (not just onnxruntime) on the same obs -- matches to ~1e-5, so this is real policy behavior, not an export or inference bug.
